children: U.S. energy firms likely added a below-normal 31 billion cubic feet of natural gas into storage last week, according to the average estimate in a Reuters poll released on Wednesday.
The estimate compares with an injection of 69 bcf during the same week a year ago and an average increase for that week of 52 bcf over the past five years (2021 to 2025).
In the prior week ended August 28, energy firms added 30 bcf of gas into storage. (USOILN=ECI)

If correct, the forecast for the week ended September 4 would increase stockpiles to 3.245 trillion cubic feet. That would be about 2.6% below the same week a year ago and about 4.5% above the five-year average for the week.
The U.S. Energy Information Administration is scheduled to release its weekly storage report at 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 GMT) on Thursday.
There were 94 total degree days (TDDs) last week, above the 30-year normal of 74 TDDs for the period, data from financial firm LSEG showed.
Total degree days measure the number of degrees a day's average temperature is above or below 65 degrees Fahrenheit (18 degrees Celsius) to estimate demand to cool or heat homes and businesses.
Reuters polled 11 analysts, whose estimates ranged from injections of 22 bcf to 38 bcf, with a median increase of 33 bcf.
Early estimates for the week ending September 11 showed an average increase of 42 bcf.
That figure compares with an injection of 87 bcf during the same week last year and a five-year average increase of 74 bcf.
